title: Metric hibernation and padding experiment log
content:
Summary:

This doc captures a set of experiments and on-call observations around a class of problems we've started calling "metric hibernation": metrics that go quiet for long stretches (minutes->hours) and then either spike or resume at previous levels, producing multi-stage alert churn and unexpected SLO burn. The goal here is to record small experiments (padding/synthesis, holdback/debounce windows, downstream padding) and a proposed lightweight runbook change so oncall can triage faster and avoid noisy escalations.

Where we saw it:
- Primary surface: kvcache miss/exporter pipeline (observability team) but also seen in: auth-service request-success-rate, router-per-route-latency histograms (partial shards), and third-party dependency exporters.
- Typical pattern: metric emits normally -> long quiet (no points) -> sudden catch-up (bunch of points) OR resume with a slightly different label set -> SLO alert triggers then recovers after backlog drains.

Why it matters:
- Oncall time wasted diagnosing downstream system outages when root cause is exporter batching/backpressure or ephemeral telemetry client GC.
- SLOs (p99 latency and availability) get burned by transient lack of datapoints because our SLO calc treats missing as errors for a 5m window in several buckets.

Quick examples observed in last 30 days (anonymized):
- auth-service: 3h hibernation due to exporter process restarting under OOM; on resume, spike in error rate from batched backlog -> 2 triggered incidents, 1 PagerDuty escalation.
- kvcache: intermittent exporter stall under high CPU pressure. Missing heartbeat metric led to unnecessary failover enactment in a downstream automation.

Data snapshots: (high level)
- Metric "service.request_success_ratio" missing points frequency: baseline 0.5% of series/day -> observed 3.2% on 2024-09-17
- Median hibernation length during incidents: ~22 minutes (Q3 sampling)
- Number of SLO alerts that had missing-data component in last 60 days: 18 (we correlated via alert tags)

Hypotheses for root causes (ranked):
1) Exporter batching with stall/retry and no synthetic heartbeat -> long gaps (most frequent)
2) Telemetry client OOM or GC pause in a few services (less frequent but longer gaps)
3) Network policy reconfiguration causing drop for a subset of hosts -> abrupt resume with partial labels
4) Scrape/ingest backpressure in the collector when ingestion RT spikes

What we tried (experiments):
A) Local padded heartbeat in exporter (padding): emit a small synthetic datapoint (value=0.0001 or event=heartbeat=true) every 30s if no real points emitted.
  - Goal: keep series visibility alive for SLO calcs and alert windows without altering downstream aggregates much.
  - Implementation: instrumentation change in telemetry helper lib (PR 236).
  - Result: reduced SLO fires caused by missing-data for services in canary group; one false positive still occurred because padded metric had slightly different label set.

B) Holdback debounce window in alerting rules: require >2 datapoints across 90s before firing on series that historically show bursty recovery patterns.
  - Added to a subset of SLO rules (90s debounce, 30% relative change threshold).
  - Result: significantly fewer short-lived alerts but introduced 20–30s additional detection latency for real regressions. Team feedback: acceptable for non-critical SLOs, NOT for critical auth path.

C) Downstream padding at collector: synthesize a 0-value when series missing in a 1m scrape if the series was present in previous scrape.
  - This was a collector-side experiment (feature flagged) on staging.
  - Result: made Grafana dashboards smoother; reduced manual triage for oncall. Need to measure long-term SLO impact.

D) Adaptive alert scoring: mark alerts with "missing-data-suspected" tag if series had >60% gap historically; route to SRE-low-priority queue.
  - Early trial reduced PD escalations but added manual overhead to annotate false-negatives afterwards.

Open questions / risks:
- Padding semantics: what values are safe? 0 vs NaN vs tiny epsilon. 0 will bias ratios downward; epsilon risks being counted as real tokens in rate sums. Need standard across teams.
- Label fidelity: if exporter resumes with label drift (new pod name), padding may create multiple series and not prevent alerting.
- SLO calculus: should missing datapoints default to OK, Unknown, or carry-over last-value? Changing SLO semantics affects thousands of alerts.
- Legal/compliance: synthetic datapoints must be flagged for auditing for customers who ingest telemetry into their systems.

Proposed short-term runbook changes (for oncall):
1) Add initial triage checklist for suspected hibernation:
   - Check series cardinality over last 30m (quick query). Command: "promql: count_over_time(<metric>[30m]) by (instance)" (adapt per metric).
   - If series shows >1m gap but host/container healthy: check exporter logs for OOM/restart.
   - Check collector metrics for backpressure: collector_exporter_queue_length and ingestion_retries.
   - If resumption pattern (burst) AND collector queue drain in last 5m -> mark incident as "telemetry-backlog" and route to observability team.
2) If alert is SLO-critical (auth, billing): disable debounce temporarily and treat normally.
3) If padding or synthetic-heartbeat is deployed for that service (flagged in service metadata): mark incident as "likely-padding" to avoid PD escalation, but still create ticket for long-term fix.

Longer-term proposals to consider:
- Standardized heartbeat field/label for all exporters (heartbeat=true) and centralized config for interval and epsilon value.
- Collector-side optional gap-filling with provenance header (so consumers see "synthesized=true").
- SLO engine change: treat missing datapoints as last-known-good for up to X minutes, configurable per SLO, with audit trail.
- Instrumentation library: add guard rails for label drift to preserve canonical series identity (reduce new-series-on-resume).

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: roll out padding lib to 5 canary services + validate label stability (target 2024-10-08).
- Jon: adjust alert debounce rules for non-critical SLOs and run 2-week experiment window (JIRA SRE-1198).
- Marta: add provenance headers for synthesized points in collector prototype (PR linked).
- Ethan: postmortem template update to include "metric hibernation" checkbox and root cause classification.

Notes to self / rough timeline:
- Week 1: canary padding + dashboards to show before/after
- Week 2: collector padding flag on staging, plus alert debounce for 30% of SLO rules
- Week 3: review PD escalations and SLO burn trends, decide on broader rollout

Links / references (quick):
- Slack thread: #observability (link pinned on Confluence-4821 page)
- Jira: SRE-1198 (debounce experiment)
- GitHub: telemetry PR 236 (padding lib)
- Confluence: Observability signal taxonomy (CONFLUENCE-4821)

Unresolved TODOs (short):
- Decide on canonical padding value and label schema (Aisha + infra-observability).
- Add synthesized=true header to collector events (Marta).
- Vet SLO engine semantics change with product and legal (scheduled 2024-10-10).

If you're oncall and see a weird burst+gap pattern, follow the triage checklist above and tag me (@aisha) in the incident. If you think a particular service is a good padding canary, add to comment section and I'll add it to the rollout list.

End of log.
